Operating System Concepts: Filesystems and Inodes

In Unix and Linux filesystems, an inode (index node) is a data structure that stores metadata about a file or directory. 
The inode contains attributes such as file size, owner user ID, group ID, file permissions, creation, modification, and access timestamps.
Crucially, the inode does not store the actual file content or the file name. The file name is mapped to the inode number inside a directory entry.
